When citizens are called to testify before congress, they aren't hooked up to a lie detector machine. But Congress still wants to know whether they are telling the truth or not. And there are a few ways to scientifically evaluate whether or not they are without needing to hook them up to a machine.

If you've ever been called to serve on an actual jury and gone through the selection process, where the prosecution and the defense have an opportunity to question and dismiss potential jurors to eliminate anyone who might not be able to fairly judge the matter at hand, has preexisting bias etc, then you might have experienced something similar to what I think McCain was trying to do. The prosecutor might say something to you that seems like a question but is worded in a way that really throws you off; he isn't really looking for your answer, but your body language as you sit there in front of a bunch of people, in that uncomfortable silence, feeling that people expect you to answer a question you can't really make sense of. Something like "What do you think people lie how would you know?" followed by an expecting silence. The prosecutor really wants to know your body language as you try to piece together that nonsense. If you yourself are lying about your capacity to judge the case without bias, then your response will likely be a stuttering mess.

Now, you can watch McCain's bizarre questioning of Comey here: https://youtu.be/-gZ8JSpcHD8

If we are trying to determine how truthful Comey is being in his testimony, more insight into what he really knows and does not know, then we want to catch on camera his real 'confused face', body language, tone and rhythm of verbal response, etc. All this can be analyzed by computers later. Crazy old McCain's questions get invoke Comey's real confused face, as they are really confusing, and then those reactions are compared to Comey's reactions to questions that HE SHOULD have been confused by if he was being entirely honest and didn't have knowledge beyond what Congress expected he should have.

In other words, if I ask Comey a real question he should be confused by, but he only pretends to be confused, then I can know that he was only pretending by comparing that response to his response to the bizarre questions from McCain that he really was confused by.

The whole hearing should be viewed as somewhat scripted. It isn't the case that each Senator comes up with their own questions they individually ask. But rather the whole line of questioning is scripted to unveil the truth by invoking and capturing and comparing different responses to different questions. Each senator is then given their own part of the script and plays their role in the theater of it all. Only the testifier isn't in on the act, and if he is acting, then the real actors will know.
